solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Palatine Rome plays host to emperor

indicators.note: the words Palatine Rome play host to, holding inside them, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Rome's Palatine Hill, home of the imperial palaces, entertains one of its rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a first-century Roman ruler, the last of the Julio-Claudian line.

clue.text: Beginning to feel stiff and cold

indicators.note: the beginning of the word feel is its opening letter alone

parts.note: stiff means rigid, unbending

explanation.surface: Someone starting to go numb and chilled, perhaps on a winter walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid is a formal synonym for icy, bitterly chilly.

clue.text: Snake swallows ant's head very quickly

indicators.note: the snake word swallows, taking inside it, the other piece

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's

indicators.note: the head of ant's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A snake gulps an insect down in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for 'as soon as possible' means with all speed, immediately.

clue.text: Red mark of omission surrounds line

indicators.note: the mark of omission surrounds, goes round, the line abbreviation

parts.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where something has been left out

explanation.surface: A proofreader's red-ink caret drawn round a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is a red Bordeaux wine, and by extension a deep purplish-red colour.

clue.text: Traitor in Paris who has support

parts.note: the French for who is qui
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: A collaborator in occupied Paris who has backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidkun Quisling, the Norwegian collaborator, gave his name to any traitor who aids an occupying enemy.

clue.text: After refurbishment, the Co-op in centre of Wigan is striking

indicators.note: a refurbished shop is rearranged, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of Wigan is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A Co-op supermarket in Wigan looks impressive after a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After refurbishment' is the anagram signal; Wigan is a town in north-west England, and 'in' joins the fodder rather than signalling insertion. 'Striking' must be read as good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone photogenic looks attractive, striking, in pictures.

clue.text: New currency is creating anxiety

parts.note: euros, plural, are the European currency, as in money held in euros
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new currency launch is making people nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety, or loosely an obsessive worry.

clue.text: 'Apollo! Horus! Ra!' being chanted, becomes dangerously high

parts.note: a chanted name is sung
ODs, overdoses, is to take a dangerous quantity of a drug

explanation.surface: Chanting the names of solar deities sends the worshippers into a dangerous frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a list of examples: Apollo (Greek), Horus and Ra (Egyptian) were all solar deities.
explanation.definitionFit: Each named figure is a deity linked with the sun, so together they are examples of the type.

clue.text: Ghouls swirling about lakes in Eire

indicators.note: ghouls swirling about are moving round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Phantoms swirl around Irish waters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lough is the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, like the Scottish loch.

clue.text: Drink, drink and drink again!

parts.note: nog is a strong beer, or an eggnog
gin is another drink, the third in the clue

explanation.surface: A drinker's rallying cry to keep on drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small measure of spirits, a quarter of a pint, so a drink.

clue.text: Sycophant disguised as pirate

indicators.note: disguised letters are given a new appearance, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A flatterer in a pirate costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite in the figurative sense is a hanger-on who lives off others by flattery.

clue.text: Most of merchandise free but useless

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its final letter

parts.note: goods are merchandise, wares
something free costs nothing, you get it at no charge

explanation.surface: Most of the stock is being given away, but it is all rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless person or thing is described with this hyphenated adjective meaning of no use.

clue.text: Icon Times destroyed, describing knight being a know-it-all

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so the shuffled letters encircle the knight
destroyed letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A smashed icon and a newspaper report about a knight who thinks he knows everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is part of the fodder, not the newspaper. 'Know-it-all' works as an adjective here: all-knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be omniscient is to have infinite knowledge, to know everything.

clue.text: Stocking many London stores

indicators.note: many London stores, keeps within, the letters required

explanation.surface: Plenty of London shops carry hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking' is a noun for the material of hosiery, not the verb about shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, named after the synthetic fibre they are made from.

clue.text: Cut tail off bird

indicators.note: with its tail off, the bird loses its final letter

parts.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A cruel instruction to dock a bird's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors.

clue.text: Old college has good fortune to be multilingual

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a type of British college abolished in 1992
one's lot is one's fortune, fate

explanation.surface: A former polytechnic is lucky enough to have students speaking many languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot person speaks several languages fluently.

clue.text: Ointment starts to soothe angry lesions — very effective

indicators.note: the starts of the five words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A cream that soothes inflamed sores and works well.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing ointment applied to wounds or sore skin.

clue.text: Remove hair by installing current in electronic metal sheet

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: installing puts the current symbol inside the other pieces

parts.note: a plate is a thin sheet of metal
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electrical depilation gadget with a metal plate and a current running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To epilate is to take hair off the body at the root, by waxing or electrolysis.

clue.text: Wilder inheritance factor?

definitions.meaning: the American comic actor ... Wilder, star of Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory
the unit of heredity passed from parent to offspring

explanation.surface: Asking whether a wilder streak is inherited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like a comparative adjective but is the surname of the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Genes are the units on chromosomes that transmit inherited traits; the actor's first name supplies the other sense.

clue.text: Securing name for international field of science renewed belief in one's abilities

indicators.note: renewed letters are made over, rearranged into a fresh order
securing here means obtaining, so the new letter is brought in
for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting an international name in a scientific field restores one's self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: In FIELD OF SCIENCE one I is swapped for N, then 'renewed' shuffles all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assurance, trust in one's own powers and judgement, is what the hyphenated phrase names.

clue.text: One selecting paint we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word said aloud that sounds like the answer

parts.note: colour is paint, as in a tin of colour

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a shade of paint from a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A culler picks out animals or items from a group, so is one who selects.

clue.text: Decorate letter by employer

parts.note: em is the spelt-out name of the letter M
a boss is one's employer

explanation.surface: A boss honoured with a letter of commendation.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to ornament a surface with a raised design.

clue.text: Extraordinary individual

definitions.meaning: remarkable, exceptional, out of the ordinary
single, one only, as opposed to plural in grammar

explanation.surface: Praise for a remarkable person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both remarkable and single, the grammatical number for one item.

clue.text: Blast animals

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of annoyance, like damn
rodents, plural, like mice but bigger

explanation.surface: Cursing at some creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an oath of irritation and also the plural of a common rodent.

clue.text: Song at sunrise offered to the French at first

indicators.note: at first places the French word ahead of the other piece

parts.note: au is French for to the
bade is an old past tense of bid, meaning offered

explanation.surface: A dawn serenade presented to the French in the first instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a poem or piece of music greeting the dawn, often of lovers parting.

clue.text: River fish

definitions.meaning: a river in Devon, south-west England
another name for the dace, a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A river and its fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Devon river and, regionally, a small freshwater fish, the dace.

clue.text: Bridge opponents with energy welcoming my call to play again?

indicators.note: the outer pieces welcome, take inside, the exclamation

parts.note: in bridge East and North are opponents, sitting in different partnerships
E is the physics symbol for energy
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A card player's opponents energetically demanding another game.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a colloquial British cry of surprise, matching 'my!'. The question mark warns that play means perform, not deal cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience shouts for an extra performance with this French-derived cry.

clue.text: Queen's hugged by terribly austere and valued friend

indicators.note: the queen is hugged by, held inside, the shuffled letters
terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A monarch embraced by a stern but cherished companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure is a much-loved, highly prized person, as in 'my housekeeper is a treasure'.
